LUNG CANCER SCREENING - LOW DOSE CT
Technique: non-contrast LDCT, 1 mm reconstructions.
Findings: Lungs are clear. Airways patent. No pulmonary nodule is seen. Mediastinum unremarkable.
Impression: Lung-RADS 1. Next screen in 12 months.
Screening LDCT thorax. No nodules, no masses, no consolidation, no effusion. No suspicious finding. Final category: Lung-RADS 1 - negative.

Baseline low-dose CT. Mild centrilobular emphysema in the upper lobes. No nodule. Mild coronary artery calcification noted - for GP review.
Lung-RADS: 1S.
Annual LDCT.

LDCT chest (annual round 3). Compared with the 2025 study, which was reported as Lung-RADS 2 because of a new 4 mm solid nodule, that nodule is no longer visible; nothing new. Overall assessment this year: Lung-RADS category 1.
LDCT SCREEN | Result: LR-1 | Nodules: none | Recommendation: routine 12-month LDCT.
Low dose chest CT, screening programme. There is no pulmonary nodule and no feature to suggest Lung-RADS 3, 4A, 4B or 4X. Lungs and pleura are normal. Overall: negative screen (Lung-RADS 1).

LDCT chest screening. Impression: the study is NOT Lung-RADS 3 or 4 - there is no significant finding. A completely calcified granuloma (3 mm) in the left lower lobe is a benign calcification. Lung-RADS 1. See you next year.

LDCT lung screening. Solid nodule right lower lobe, 3.5 mm mean diameter, unchanged since the prior round. Perifissural nodule left, 4 mm, smooth, triangular. Both benign appearance.
Impression: Lung-RADS 2 (benign appearance or behaviour). Continue annual screening.

Screening CT chest (low dose). Calcified granuloma in the right upper lobe. Solid nodule left lower lobe 4.5 mm, smooth. No other nodule.
Final: LungRADS 2.

LDCT screening, baseline. Solid nodule left upper lobe measuring 5.6 mm mean diameter (below the 6 mm threshold for category 3 on a baseline scan). No suspicious features.
Lung-RADS category 2.
Repeat at 12 months.
LDCT. 5 mm ground-glass nodule right middle lobe, unchanged compared with the previous year (non-solid nodules under 30 mm are category 2). Conclusion: Lung-RADS 2. Annual screening.

Low-dose CT for lung cancer screening: small subpleural nodule 3 mm, stable. There is no suspicious nodule, no spiculated mass and no lymphadenopathy. Lung-RADS: 2S (moderate emphysema). Next LDCT in 12 months.
LDCT screening result - category: 2 (Lung-RADS v2022). Findings: scattered solid nodules all under 6 mm, smooth. Action: annual.
Annual LDCT. A 2022 study had Lung-RADS 4A for a nodule that has since resolved completely. Today: a stable 3 mm solid nodule in the lingula and linear scarring; nothing else. Lung-RADS 2.

Low-dose CT lung screening. Comparison: 2024 - Lung-RADS 4B; subsequent PET and biopsy showed organising pneumonia (benign) and the area has now resolved. Today: 4 mm solid nodule right apex, new but under 6 mm. Overall Lung-RADS 2. (Do not apply the 2024 category.)
Annual LDCT. A new solid nodule 3.8 mm mean diameter right lower lobe (new nodules below 4 mm are category 2). Otherwise normal lungs. Lung-RADS 2.
Low dose CT lung cancer screening. Solid nodule 4 mm, benign appearance. Final assessment: Lung-RADS two (benign). Annual screening to continue.
LDCT screening. Examination is incomplete: respiratory motion artefact in the lower zones limits assessment; additional imaging is needed. Lung-RADS 0. Recall for a repeat limited LDCT.

Low-dose CT chest, baseline screening. Several nodules cannot be characterised without the prior CT from an outside hospital, which has been requested. Category: Lung-RADS 0 (comparison with prior imaging pending). Result will be finalised on receipt.
Screening LDCT. Part of the left lower lobe is obscured by dense atelectasis, so a nodule cannot be excluded there. Not a negative screen. Lung-RADS 0 - repeat LDCT in 1-3 months.
LDCT SCREEN | Result: category 0 | Reason: infectious/inflammatory process suspected, treat and repeat LDCT 1-3 months | Not reportable as negative.
LDCT screening. Technically limited by patient motion. The radiologist notes that if the repeat shows no nodule, this would be Lung-RADS 1, but until then the category is 0 (incomplete).

Baseline LDCT. Solid nodule right upper lobe, mean diameter 7.2 mm, smooth margins. Probably benign.
Impression: Lung-RADS 3. Short-interval LDCT in 6 months.
LDCT screening. Part-solid nodule left lower lobe, total diameter 8 mm, solid component 4 mm (under 6 mm). Overall Lung-RADS category 3, six month LDCT advised.

Annual LDCT. The referral form queries Lung-RADS 4 because of a family history of lung cancer, which does not change the category. Imaging: 7 mm solid nodule left apex, newly seen on this round (new nodules of 4 mm to under 8 mm are category 3). A separate 2 mm calcified granuloma is benign. Final: Lung-RADS 3.
LDCT SCREEN - LR 3 - probably benign - repeat LDCT 6 mo.

Low-dose lung screening CT. 30 mm non-solid ground-glass nodule right upper lobe, new on this scan. No solid component, no spiculation, no lymphadenopathy. Lung-RADS 3 (non-solid nodule of 30 mm or more). Recommend LDCT at 6 months.

Annual LDCT. Solid nodule right middle lobe now 9 mm, previously 5 mm: growth of 4 mm. Suspicious. Lung-RADS 4A. Diagnostic CT or 3-month LDCT; PET/CT may be considered for 8 mm or larger solid component.
Baseline LDCT. Solid nodule left lower lobe, mean diameter 9.5 mm. Impression: Lung-RADS 4A - recommend LDCT in 3 months, PET/CT if solid component 8 mm or more.
Screening LDCT. Subsolid nodule right upper lobe 14 mm with 7 mm solid component. A separate 4 mm solid nodule is category 2. The overall exam takes the more concerning finding: Lung-RADS 4A.
LDCT SCREEN RESULT | Lung-RADS 4A | Suspicious | Follow-up LDCT in 3 months.
Low dose CT thorax. New solid nodule 8.5 mm right lower lobe (new nodules of 8 mm or more and under 15 mm are category 4A). No lymphadenopathy, no spiculation, no features of 4X. Final category: 4A.
Screening low-dose CT. Solid nodule right lung, 10 mm. Final assessment given in words: category four A, suspicious. Three-month follow-up LDCT recommended.
Baseline LDCT. Solid nodule left upper lobe 17 mm, spiculated. Very suspicious. Lung-RADS 4B. Refer for chest physician review, tissue sampling and/or PET/CT.
Annual screening CT. Solid nodule right lower lobe grown from 10 mm to 16 mm. Lung-RADS category 4B. Urgent referral to the lung multidisciplinary team.
LDCT SCREEN | category 4B | Solid 15 mm+ | Action: diagnostic work-up within 30 days.
Low dose CT. Part-solid nodule 22 mm, solid component 10 mm. Prior LDCT a year ago was Lung-RADS 2 (no nodule at that site). This represents a new, very suspicious lesion. Overall: Lung-RADS 4B.
Annual LDCT. Large solid nodule left lower lobe 28 mm. Lung-RADS category four B - very suspicious. Immediate referral.

Screening LDCT. Spiculated 12 mm solid nodule right upper lobe with ipsilateral enlarged hilar lymph nodes, 18 mm short axis. Category 4 with additional suspicious features: Lung-RADS 4X. Urgent multidisciplinary team referral.
LDCT SCREEN | 4X | nodule with additional features suspicious for lung cancer (lymphadenopathy, pleural thickening) | refer urgently.
Annual LDCT. Previously Lung-RADS 3 (7 mm nodule). The nodule is now 11 mm, with a new pleural-based nodule and an enlarged subcarinal node (16 mm). Overall assessment: Lung-RADS category 4X.
